query_text: Are there any academic fields that don't have enough people trying to teach?

annotations.title: Teacher Shortages by Subjects Across States | Learning Policy Institute
Most U.S. public elementary and secondary schools faced hiring challenges for the start of the 2024–25 academic year | IES

content.text:
Yes—but it depends a lot on whether you mean **K–12 teaching** or **college/university teaching**.

## If you mean K–12 school subjects

In the U.S., the clearest shortages are usually in:

- **Special education**
- **Math**
- **Science**, especially physics, chemistry, and sometimes computer science
- **English as a second language / bilingual education**
- **World languages / foreign languages**
- **Career and technical education** — e.g., trades, health occupations, technology
- Sometimes **speech-language pathology**, school psychology, and other student-support roles

For 2024–25 data, the Learning Policy Institute reported that states most commonly identified shortages in **special education — 45 states**, **science — 41 states**, and **math — 40 states**. Other widespread shortage areas included language arts, world languages, career and technical education, ESL, and social studies. ([learningpolicyinstitute.org](https://learningpolicyinstitute.org/product/teacher-shortages-subjects-across-states-factsheet?utm_source=openai))

NCES/IES also found that among schools with vacancies, many reported difficulty filling roles such as **special education**, **ESL/bilingual education**, **foreign languages**, **math**, and **computer science** for the 2024–25 school year. ([ies.ed.gov](https://ies.ed.gov/learn/press-release/most-u-s-public-elementary-and-secondary-schools-faced-hiring-challenges-start-2024-25-academic-year?utm_source=openai))

## If you mean college/university teaching

There usually is **not** a broad shortage of people who want to be professors. In many humanities and social-science fields, there are often **far more PhDs than tenure-track jobs**.

But some applied fields can have real shortages because people with the right credentials can earn more outside academia. Common examples include:

- **Nursing faculty**
- **Accounting**
- **Computer science**
- **Engineering**
- **Some health professions**
- **Data science / cybersecurity / AI-adjacent fields**
- **Some business fields, especially finance/accounting**

Nursing is one of the clearest examples: the American Association of Colleges of Nursing describes an ongoing **nursing faculty shortage**, partly because clinical and private-sector jobs often pay more than academic positions. ([aacnnursing.org](https://www.aacnnursing.org/news-data/fact-sheets/nursing-faculty-shortage?sfcid=7013X000002BbcUQAS%3FprogramId%3D0013X00002h826lQAA%3FprogramId%3D0013X00002h82AnQAI%3FprogramId%3D0013X00002h82BpQAI%3FprogramId%3D0013X00002h826oQAA%3FprogramId%3D0013X00002h82HZQAY%3FprogramId%3D0013X00002h82CsQAI%3FprogramId%3D0013X00002h82BpQAI%3FprogramId%3D0013X00002h826pQAA%3FprogramId%3D0013X00002h82MQQAY%3FprogramId%3D0013X00002h826lQAA%3FprogramId%3D0013X00002h82IWQAY%3FprogramId%3D0013X00002h824PQAQ%3FprogramId%3D0013X00002h82BqQAI%3FprogramId%3D0013X00002h82HZQAY%3FprogramId%3D0013X00002h824IQAQ%3FprogramId%3D0013X00002h826pQAA%3FprogramId%3D0013X00002h82MQQAY%3FprogramId%3D0013X00002h82BpQAI%3FprogramId%3D0013X00002h82ApQAI%3FprogramId%3D0013X00002h82AnQAI%3FprogramId%3D0013X00002h824JQAQ%3FprogramId%3D0013X00002h826pQAA%3FprogramId%3D0013X00002h826nQAA%3FprogramId%3D0013X00002h824PQAQ%3FprogramId%3D0013X00002h82ApQAI%3FprogramId%3D0013X00002h824PQAQ%3FprogramId%3D0013X00002h82A0QAI&utm_source=openai))

## Important caveat

“Shortage” does **not** always mean “easy, well-paid job.” It can mean:

- schools can’t find certified teachers in certain subjects;
- rural or high-poverty districts have trouble hiring;
- salaries are not competitive with industry;
- working conditions drive people away;
- universities rely on adjuncts rather than creating full-time faculty jobs.

So the short answer is: **yes, especially special education, math, science, ESL/bilingual education, world languages, career/technical education, nursing, accounting, computer science, engineering, and some health fields.** But shortages are highly dependent on **state, district, institution type, and credential level**.
